object_description: fragmented stepped volume with an articulated radiating plan
design_condition: The compact, stepped building follows the inhabited hillside, preserves the beech and existing plant structure, and forms distinct gardens and undergrowth spaces around its entrances.

positive.statement: The project fits simply and naturally into the topographical and landscape context through its relatively small footprint.
The articulated and radiating plan avoids long built fronts and contributes to good integration into the site.
The fragmented volume is precisely articulated with neighboring buildings while preserving and highlighting the beech.
The entrances are clearly identifiable as extensions of adjoining exterior spaces and support easy separation of access.
The relationship between the two halls offers visual transparency throughout the building.
The circulation devices are generous and spatially rich, and the program is laid out efficiently.
The project is rational and economical while respecting regulatory constraints.

negative.statement: The skylights narrow and suggest insufficient natural light in the lower-floor halls.
The relatively high height of the building, coupled with the reduced attic skylights, limits daylight penetration into the lower floors.
